items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 4.7.3 at source lines 677-680: if g is a retract of f then every fiber of g is a retract of the corresponding fiber of f. The author's proof (source lines 682-705) is an explicit construction whose difficulty is entirely in the coherence data: the two maps between fibers have to be written down using all five pieces of the retraction record (lines 685-688), the retraction identity is then reduced by reordering the Pis and applying the omission-of-contractible-components result to the single case p = refl (lines 693-699), and the remaining obstruction is an equality of pairs that is split by the sigma-path characterisation (line 700) and closed only after computing the transport as opp(g(R a)) `ct` K(s a) `ct` r'(L a) `ct` R'(g a) and matching it against the coherence homotopy H(a) (lines 702-704). The statement mentions none of these components.
